 Hawaii sets new record in 116-44 win against Bethesda 
 Hawaii finished opening night of the Rainbow Classic with a 116-44 win against Bethesda University Friday. By HNN Staff Published : Nov. 6, 2026 at 11:39 PM HST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - The University of Hawaii Rainbow Warrior men’s basketball team set a new record for the largest margin of victory with a 72-point win against Bethesda University.
 On Friday, the ‘Bows took to the court against the Lion Angels for the 60th annual Outrigger Rainbow Classic at Bankoh Arena at the Stan Shierff Center, and finished opening night with a final score of 116-44.
 Hawaii gained an early lead after a dunk from guard Tanner Cuff tied the game in the early minutes and the ‘Bows kept the momentum into the half, leading 61-21.
 “I was just trying to make a play, get downhill and the lane opened right up, so I was like, I’m going to go up and score,” he said.
 Cuff finished the night with 14 points, five of six from the field with four rebounds and two assists.
 All eleven players who suited up for the ‘Bows Friday scored.
 “That’s what you like to see,” said ‘Bows head coach Eran Ganot. “I said at halftime, we didn’t like our first 10 minutes. We were playing too soft, too passive, but we started playing like a team. Proud of the way they finished the half and played in the second, and played guys who deserve to play who’ve been supporting other guys that’d been supporting other guys.”
 Ganot earned his 200th win as a head coach. He is three away from his 200th win with Hawaii.
 “That part is humbling,” he said.
 The ‘Bows’ win eclipses the previous record of 67 points set in a 110-43 win over BYU Hawaii on Nov. 20, 1962. It’s also the fourth-highest total in program history.
 Hawaii returns to the court Sunday against UT Arlington at 5 p.m. Coverage on K5 begins with the ‘Bows Pregame Show at 4:30 p.m.
